name: Video game
task: art-directing, prompting or building the look of a game world: its camera, geometry, surfaces, palette, light and the rooms and streets the player moves through
description: Video game styles as visual rules, not as genres or stories. Each style is a set of hardware limits or art-direction choices that make one look of a world: the projection, the polygon or pixel budget, the colour depth, the light model and how rooms and streets are built for a player to move through. The domain is a source for immersive interior and exterior work: a game world is architecture that a person walks through on a screen.

vectors.label: Render fidelity
vectors.low: a few pixels or lines that suggest a thing

vectors.label: Spatial depth
vectors.high: a free camera in a full 3D world

vectors.label: Lighting drama
vectors.high: hard contrast, volumetric beams and deep shadow

assets.purpose: One fixed scene, a village square with a house front and an open door into a lit room, in the camera, geometry, palette and light of the style.

knobs.label: Render resolution
knobs.description: The height of the internal frame before it is scaled to the display.

knobs.label: Colour depth
knobs.description: The bits for each pixel on screen: 2 for four shades, 8 for 256 colours, 24 or more for full colour.

knobs.label: Camera projection
knobs.description: How the world is projected onto the screen.

knobs.label: Shading steps
knobs.description: The number of tonal steps from the lit side to the shadow side of one surface: 1 = flat, 2 to 3 = cel, 256 = smooth.

knobs.label: Texel density
knobs.description: The texture or sprite pixels for each metre of the world.
